86867067.extract:
# Midnight Sun (Zara Larsson album)

## Lead
Midnight Sun is the fifth studio album by Swedish singer Zara Larsson, released worldwide on 26 September 2025 through her imprint Sommer House under exclusive license to Epic Records (Sony Music Entertainment). The 10‑track set blends high‑energy dance‑pop and electropop with introspective songwriting inspired by the Scandinavian “midnight sun” and Larsson’s Swedish summers. Preceded by the singles Pretty Ugly, Midnight Sun, and Crush, the album reached number one on the Swedish Albums Chart, number 36 in the United Kingdom, number 31 in Australia, and number 53 in Germany. U.S. trade outlets reported a debut at number 3 on Billboard’s Top Dance/Electronic Albums and number 22 on Top Album Sales, and listed a Billboard 200 debut at number 119. Critics in Rolling Stone, university publications, and music magazines highlighted the record’s cohesive summer aesthetic, vocal confidence, and thoughtful turns on ambition and adulthood. The album was supported by a European arena run in autumn 2025 and a North American tour planned for 2026, alongside a limited “Lisa Frank Edition” CD and clear vinyl pressings. 

## Background and development
Larsson’s release campaign and label press materials frame Midnight Sun as a project conceived around the feeling of a Swedish summer where the sun never sets—grounding the album title and its imagery. In announcing the LP, Larsson said she wanted the whole record to feel like an endless summer night, proudly drawing from her Swedish pop heritage. The title track was among the first songs written for the project. Principal collaborators include longtime partner MNEK, producers Margo XS and Zhone, and songwriter Helena Gao, with additional contributions across individual tracks. 

Rolling Stone documented Larsson’s self‑confidence entering the era—fueled by bright, Y2K‑tinged visuals that followed viral moments from earlier hits and an energetic run opening for Tate McRae—while Larsson broke down how key songs map the album’s identity, from club‑ready euphoria to more reflective pieces about purpose and adulthood. 

## Composition and lyrics
Midnight Sun is primarily dance‑pop and electropop, interlacing trance‑styled choruses, club‑leaning beats, and “Euro summer” textures with lyrical themes of romance, identity, ambition, and late‑twenties self‑reflection.

- Title track Midnight Sun opens with a melodic, dance‑forward rush and hypnotic hook, intended to capture the surreal continuity of summer daylight. 
- Blue Moon continues the buoyant mood; reviewers noted ethereal vocalizations and a dizzying pop energy. 
- Pretty Ugly leans into rowdy, chant‑like confrontation and feminist edge over stomping production. 
- Girl’s Girl explores the tension between solidarity and desire; critics observed its “messier” emotional moments as compelling. 
- Eurosummer nods to 2010s Eastern European pop staples, with playful accordion touches and a breezy Mediterranean flair. 
- Hot & Sexy celebrates feminine confidence while introducing a pointed outro about women’s safety and social responsibility, and features a re‑recorded line by television personality Tiffany Pollard. 
- The Ambition interrogates comparison and validation in the industry, pairing a catchy hook with confessional lyrics. 
- Saturn’s Return reflects late‑twenties turbulence and acceptance of uncertainty, reinforcing the album’s celestial motif. 
- Puss Puss (Swedish for “kiss kiss”) closes with playful intimacy and phone‑call imagery, balancing the set’s maximalist energy with levity. 

Apple Music’s editorial copy characterized the album as “larger, bolder, and more flamboyant” than VENUS (2024), aiming for peak dancefloor euphoria while retaining a hedonistic, sun‑soaked mood. 

## Release and promotion
Larsson announced Midnight Sun in early June 2025 alongside pre‑orders, with the title track scheduled for mid‑June and an autumn album release. The album became available globally on 26 September 2025 across digital platforms and in multiple physical formats. The roll‑out included:

- Official website and social campaigns directing fans to pre‑save the single and pre‑order the album. 
- A Sony Music Canada press release on release day summarizing collaborators, themes, and the special “Lisa Frank Edition” CD (launched in partnership with Lisa Frank, Inc.) and highlighting touring plans. 
- A limited “Lisa Frank Edition” CD and a standard CD sold via Larsson’s official store, and clear vinyl pressings, some signed or with signed art cards. 
- Music video content and editorial playlisting on DSPs; a lyric video for Midnight Sun was released in late June. 
- European arena dates announced by outlets including The Line of Best Fit, with additional socials facilitating presale access. 

## Singles and videos
- Pretty Ugly – first single of the era, released in April 2025; included on the album and referenced in label and media announcements. 
- Midnight Sun – title track and second single, released 13 June 2025; accompanied by an official lyric video; later expanded via a bundle featuring a live version and Alex Chapman remix. A collaborative single version with Muni Long also appeared on streaming services. 
- Crush – third single, issued in August 2025 and featured in release‑day press; performed at radio through late 2025. 

Scandipop named Midnight Sun its “Song of the Summer” and covered the release of the remix/live bundle in August. 

## Critical reception
Midnight Sun received generally positive notices.

- Rolling Stone praised the LP’s relentless, high‑energy joy and highlighted Larsson’s “messier” moments as the most alive, while commending the project’s reflections on ambition and adulthood. 
- A Rolling Stone feature contextualized the era’s aesthetics and momentum, and offered Larsson’s track‑by‑track insights on composition and themes. 
- University press reviews lauded the album’s cohesive summer framing and vocal confidence. The Brown Daily Herald described the record as Larsson’s most personal and cohesive work to date, mixing Euro‑pop with deepened lyricism; The Daily Nebraskan emphasized the balance of dance‑pop perfection with self‑reflection and identity. 
- Melodic Magazine called Midnight Sun Larsson’s strongest, most cohesive body of work, singling out Crush and Saturn’s Return as standouts and noting the project’s distinctive yet familiar palette. 

## Commercial performance
- Sweden: Debuted at number 1 on the Sverigetopplistan albums chart in the week dated 3 October 2025; three weeks on chart. 
- United Kingdom: Debuted at number 36 on the Official Albums Chart (week of 3–9 October 2025). 
- Australia: Debuted at number 31 on the ARIA Top 50 Albums (week commencing 6 October 2025). 
- Germany: Peaked at number 53 on the Offizielle Deutsche Charts Top 100 albums. 
- United States:
 - Trade outlets reported a career‑best debut at number 3 on Billboard’s Top Dance/Electronic Albums and number 22 on Top Album Sales, with additional Luminate/Internet Albums placements; these reports also noted Crush rising at pop radio. 
 - Third‑party chart trackers listed a Billboard 200 debut at number 119 in the week of 11 October 2025. 

As of 12 December 2025, no official certifications for the album were reported by certifying bodies; press materials highlighted catalog certifications for earlier singles. 

## Track listing and credits
All track times and principal credits per official DSP metadata; writers/composers credited as listed.

1. Midnight Sun – 3:09 (Zara Larsson, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman) 
2. Blue Moon – 3:02 (Helena Gao, Zara Larsson, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman, Kevin Hickey) 
3. Pretty Ugly – 2:38 (Zara Larsson, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman) 
4. Girl’s Girl – 2:58 (Zara Larsson, Uzoechi Emenike, Tyler Christian Lewis, Aminata Kabba, Patricio Contreras) 
5. Crush – 2:57 (Zara Larsson, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman, Kevin Hickey) 
6. Eurosummer – 2:52 (Zara Larsson, Mary Weitz, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman, Kevin Hickey, Scott Bruzenak) 
7. Hot & Sexy – 3:09 (Helena Gao, Zara Larsson, Tiffany Pollard, Uzoechi Emenike, Jon Shave, Margo Wildman, Kevin Hickey) 
8. The Ambition – 3:34 (Zara Larsson, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman) 
9. Saturn’s Return – 3:47 (Zara Larsson, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman, Kevin Hickey) 
10. Puss Puss – 3:48 (Zara Larsson, Helena Gao, Uzoechi Emenike, Margo Wildman) 

Album metadata: ℗ 2025 Sommer House, under exclusive license to Epic Records, a division of Sony Music Entertainment; total runtime approximately 31:58. 

## Personnel
Credits across the album and lead single include:

- Zara Larsson – lead and background vocals; songwriting 
- MNEK (Uzoechi Emenike) – songwriting; production (noted across album tracks and single); executive production on the single; creative direction in sessions 
- Margo XS (Margo Wildman) – songwriting; production 
- Helena Gao – songwriting 
- Zhone – production (as noted in announcement coverage) 
- Additional songwriters/creators – Kevin Hickey; Tyler Christian Lewis; Aminata Kabba; Patricio Contreras; Mary Weitz; Scott Bruzenak; Tiffany Pollard; Jon Shave (per track‑level credits) 
- Tom Norris – mixing (single Midnight Sun) 
- Kaelen Russel – engineering (single Midnight Sun) 

Full detailed roles per track (e.g., instrumentation, programming) were listed on DSP credit pages where available. 

## Formats and editions
- Digital album – standard 10‑track release on major streaming platforms. 
- CD – standard edition (U.S. and international); signed variants. 
- CD – limited “Lisa Frank Edition” (U.K. & U.S.), with collaborative artwork/packaging. 
- Vinyl – 12" clear pressings (some with signed art cards). 
Labeling and catalog details are documented across the official store and release listings. 

## Tour association
Larsson supported Midnight Sun with:

- European arena tour (October–November 2025), including Munich’s Zenith Arena, London’s OVO Arena Wembley, Amsterdam’s Ziggo Dome, and a finale at Stockholm’s Avicii Arena. 
- North American headline dates (February–April 2026) announced via label and artist channels. 
- Additional touring in 2025 included an arena run opening for Tate McRae. 

## Release history
- Worldwide (digital and physical): 26 September 2025. Some regional Apple Music pages list 25 September due to local time zones; label materials and retail pages align on 26 September. 

## Disambiguation
This article concerns the 2025 studio album Midnight Sun by Zara Larsson. Other albums titled Midnight Sun by different artists exist and are unrelated.

**(Toronto, ON — September 26,2025)**It may be the first week of fall, but for**Zara Larsson,**summer never ends. Today, the multiplatinum chart-topping global pop powerhouse releases her hotly anticipated new album,**_Midnight Sun_**. Get it[**HERE**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fzaralarsson.lnk.to%2FMidnightSun&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151150296%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=HSa9NHAxeP0427kqzr%2FYD8UHzbpP4c8E5Fx9Z88XbBA%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://zaralarsson.lnk.to/MidnightSun. Click or tap if you trust this link.")at all DSPs via**Sommer House**/**Epic Records**.

Unapologetically unfiltered and openly vulnerable, the 10-track set ripples with personal confidence and is set to a bold mix of kaleidoscopic pop and euphoric dance that complements**Zara**’s every mood. Plumbing the depths of her artistry and journey over nearly 20 years in the public eye, the album is unafraid to show all sides of the 27-year-old: lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain, often in the same breath.

Also available today is the exclusive**_Midnight Sun (Lisa Frank Edition)_**CD, a vibrant collaboration with the iconic design brand**Lisa Frank, Inc**. The limited-run package brings to life a dreamy, aquatic world inspired by the memes and moments that so many of**Zara**’s fans around the world participated in over the past year.Get it while supplies last[**HERE**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fzaralarsson.lnk.to%2FLisaFrank&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151172884%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=KQn1sHFAHFQafqk0sR3evnXwR8F2UhiHaWD3AwWuBzo%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://zaralarsson.lnk.to/LisaFrank. Click or tap if you trust this link.").

The album arrives as**Zara**approaches the finale of her arena-conquering run on**Tate McCrae**’s**Miss Possessive Tour**with back-to-back nights at**Los Angeles’ Kia Forum**starting tonight. As _Billboard_ proclaimed after a two-night run at**New York’s Madison Square Garden**, the tour has proven that**Zara’s**“_Stateside domination seems all but certain.”_ With that, she’ll headline her own**Midnight Sun Tour**starting in**Europe**this fall, with recently announced**North America**dates to follow starting in February 2026.See her global touring itinerary below go[**HERE**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.zaralarssonofficial.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151189362%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=fu4PitMgjsRhRDIChzROEzLLt7UJcHtlGeTIZLVV4CU%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: http://www.zaralarssonofficial.com/. Click or tap if you trust this link.")for tickets.

The headline tour will bring to life her most emotionally evocative and viscerally thrilling set of songs yet on**_Midnight Sun_**, which she crafted over the last year alongside songwriter**Helena Gao**and producers**MNEK**,**Margo XS**, and**Zhone.**

The previously unheard**“Blue Moon”**is an anthem for the hopeless romantics set to warm tones and heart-racing drum ’n’ bass rhythms — a celebration of timeless love. At the other end of the spectrum is**“Hot & Sexy,”**a mix of ’80s electro, ’90s house, Y2K pop, and 2010s bass music that samples**Tiffany Pollard**’s iconic _Big Brother_ rant – a charged-up “no boys allowed” anthem that evolves into a hyperpop fever dream with lyrics that dig deep beneath the surface and explore autonomy. On the introspective penultimate track “**Saturn’s Return**,”**Zara**reflects on personal growth and self-discovery, embracing uncertainty with a deeper sense of self. Paired with “**The Ambition**” right before, which explores the double-edged nature of drive and the pressures of success in modern times, the two highlight the album’s raw honesty as they explore identity, expectations, and stepping into a new era of life.

**_Midnight Sun_**’s robust set of new songs join already thriving singles like**“**[**Crush**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DZB600rRlPO8&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151204507%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=8Fvgy30ss6y7fUGbCiAR%2BKzqYWMXcIsRflNY5zBoge8%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZB600rRlPO8. Click or tap if you trust this link.")**,”**which was one of the most-added at US Top 40 radio six weeks in a row, where it is currently Top 25 on the Mediabase Pop chart and pushing Top 10 on the Mediabase Dance Radio chart.The era kicked off with the unabashedly rowdy**“**[**Pretty Ugly**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DPaddtn5IdCk&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151219599%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=5gjYmmuwJY20Xahw1nH8PuC%2BC7mku%2F3BStYRSjcUGHM%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Paddtn5IdCk. Click or tap if you trust this link.")**”**whose**Charlotte Rutherford**-directed,**Zoi Tatopoulos-**choreographed video was nominated at the 2025 MTV Video Music Awards for “Best Choreography.” And then there’s the transcendent title track,**“**[**Midnight Sun**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DuvY8fdgezLQ%26t%3D1s&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151234328%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=08w2oGZa%2Bo0nAujIMSfk1lSLfettwKYYYu%2BpYy3t36M%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uvY8fdgezLQ&t=1s. Click or tap if you trust this link.")**,”**which has been viral all summer long thanks to**Charlotte Rutherford**’s Y2K-inspired music video and**Zara**’s jaw-dropping vocal prowess. With cosigns from a wide array of fellow artists like Renee Rapp, PinkPanthress and Ariana Grande, the press has rallied around the track, with _Rolling Stone_ calling it a _“song-of-the-summer contender”_ right out of the gate._PAPER dubbed it_ a _“shimmering pop anthem soaked in nostalgia,”_ while _GRAMMY.com_ wrote _“the beat drops with such hypnotic force that the track’s climax feels like staring directly into, well, a midnight sun.”_**_Pitchfork_**, however, summed up what we are all thinking: “_Midnight Sun is simply too much my shit!”_

_“Throughout Midnight Sun,”_**Zara****Larsson**says, “_I get to just capture that total Scandinavian vibe, which is something that I have grown up with—it’s a huge part of me, my happiest memories and my saddest ones, too. A part of my soul is a Swedish summer night. This record encompasses that.”_

Now, as the fires of anticipation reach a blinding blaze,**Zara Larsson**’s never-ending**_Midnight Sun_**is, at last, here — and here to stay.

_“It just feels like me—knowing myself, this album is just really, really me. And also,”_**Zara**says with a grin, “_No one can do me the way I can.”_

**About Zara Larsson**

On her fourth studio album,_Midnight Sun_, Swedish pop sensation Zara Larsson had a goal: “I wanted the whole album to feel like it’s a summer night and it never ends,” she says. “A part of my soul is a Swedish summer night. This record encompasses that, how life is so beautiful it makes you cry.” Once she put together her team of collaborators — “Never Forget You” collaborator MNEK, up-and-coming producer Margo XS, and songwriter Helena Gao — the core four got to work. On day one, they made lead singles “Midnight Sun” and lead single “Pretty Ugly,” realizing quickly that there was magic in the room. They felt an energy that connected them, emboldening her to be open, vulnerable, raw, and real.

_Midnight Sun_ ripples with that same confidence and trust. Its storytelling bursts with truth and vulnerability, plumbing the depth and growth of Zara’s artistry and journey over nearly 20 years in the public eye. It’s an album unafraid to show all sides of the 27-year-old: lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain, often in the same breath._Midnight Sun_ follows Zara’s first three albums (2017’s _So Good_, 2021’s _Poster Girl_, and last year’s _VENUS_), building upon her legacy while taking things back to her roots. “Making this album brought me back to the very beginning, my first EPs when I started making music, because it was all about having fun and just creating and speaking honestly,” she says. “The people who will love this album will love a very true part of me.”

Midnight Sun
============

[Zara Larsson](https://music.apple.com/us/artist/zara-larsson/570372593)

POP · 2025

Swedish pop phenom Zara Larsson has spent her career steadily building towards a point of pure dance-floor ecstasy, and her fifth album _Midnight Sun_ represents the point where she’s seemingly finally reached the summit. Executive-produced by British dance-pop wizard MNEK, the follow-up to 2024’s _VENUS_ is bigger, brasher, and more audacious than its predecessor. A clear point of comparison is the total head-rush pop of fellow Swede Tove Lo, only instead of neon-lit clubs, the locale is the sweltering, sandy beach environ evoked in the indelible “Eurosummer.” Hedonism is the name of the game across _Midnight Sun_: Just check out the zippy synths that stomp down the catwalk of “Hot & Sexy” or the low-riding and “Hollaback Girl”-recalling crunk of “Pretty Ugly.” Even the more subtle moments here—the skyscraping pop of “Blue Moon,” the perfectionist’s-lament sweep of “The Ambition”—feel jam-packed with sound, a true reflection of a pop star pushing her music to the limits and then some.

7.content:
It ended up becoming our Song of the Summer after **[it came out](https://scandipop.co.uk/song-zara-larsson-midnight-sun/)** just under two months ago, now Zara Larsson is extending our weeks of midnight sunshine via two new versions of her hit – **[a remix by Alex Chapman](https://open.spotify.com/track/1LFBygPkUZyFE0U7hJDWOb?si=75c0b2aa6f6c4a6b)** and a Live Version. The latter is so much more than its title suggests, however. Stripped back, slowed down and serving as an incredible showcase of her vocals. That moment at the end of the second chorus…. Prepare yourself!

Zara Larsson announces fourth album, Midnight Sun
=================================================

06 June 2025, 11:29 | Written by [Tyler Damara Kelly](https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/authors/tkelly)

 ([News](https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news)) 

[(Zara Larsson)](https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/artists/zara-larsson)[(Album release news)](https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/tags/release-news)

Multi-platinum artist [Zara Larsson](https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/artists/zara-larsson) has announced the release of her forthcoming album, _Midnight Sun_.

“In thinking about this album, I thought, ‘What do I want to say? What do I want this to be?’ I really am proud of my Swedish pop heritage, so I wanted to write about a Swedish summer where the sun never goes down,” says Zara. “And it doesn't matter if it's December: the summer night will be there for you. It's waiting for you, it will come back for you, and you will come back for it.”

Zara Larsson has also announced a European arena tour for autumn – the first official leg of her _Midnight Sun Tour._ It will kick off in Munich, Germany on 28 October at Zenith Arena, which leads her to conquer London’s OVO Arena, Wembley, Amsterdam’s Ziggo Dome, followed by a run of Nordic arenas culminating in a homecoming show at Avicii Arena in Stockholm, Sweden on 28 November.

_Midnight Sun_, is set for release on 26 September, and is [available to pre-order now](https://forms.sonymusicfans.com/campaign/midnightsun-presave/). The title track will be released on 13 June.

‘Midnight Sun’ is the shining light of Zara Larsson’s discography
=================================================================

The singer’s fifth album both distinguishes itself from and fits in with her former work.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 3: The album cover from "Midnight Sun," which shows Zara Larsson in an orange dress with light pouring through trees behind her.](https://snworksceo.imgix.net/bdh/a39982d0-2876-4627-94b8-516d2009d38d.sized-1000x1000.jpg?w=1000)

“Midnight Sun,” which comes 17 years into Larsson’s career, is markedly more personal than her previous work.

Courtesy of Charlotte Rutherford via Sony Music Canada

 By [Camilla Rodriguez](https://www.browndailyherald.com/staff/camilla-rodriguez)

Contributing Writer 

October 13, 2025 | 11:29pm EDT

*   [](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2025/10/midnight-sun-is-the-shining-light-of-zara-larssons-discography)
*   [](http://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2025/10/midnight-sun-is-the-shining-light-of-zara-larssons-discography&text=%E2%80%98Midnight%20Sun%E2%80%99%20is%20the%20shining%20light%20of%20Zara%20Larsson%E2%80%99s%20discography)
*   [](mailto:?subject=%E2%80%98Midnight%20Sun%E2%80%99%20is%20the%20shining%20light%20of%20Zara%20Larsson%E2%80%99s%20discography%20|%20The%20Brown%20Daily%20Herald&text=Check%20out%20this%20article%20from%20The%20Brown%20Daily%20Herald%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.browndailyherald.com%2Farticle%2F2025%2F10%2Fmidnight-sun-is-the-shining-light-of-zara-larssons-discography)
*   [](https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2025/10/midnight-sun-is-the-shining-light-of-zara-larssons-discography#)

On Sept. 26, Swedish singer Zara Larsson released “Midnight Sun,” her fifth studio album. Marked by its bright, Malibu Barbie aesthetic, the album is meant to evoke the feeling of a Swedish summer, as evidenced by its title, which [references](https://youtu.be/WFzcodGYcHQ?si=c7mpHrg94VjXwaiP&t=64) the long periods of daylight Sweden experiences in the summer.

“Midnight Sun,” which comes 17 years into Larsson’s career, is markedly more personal than her previous work. Produced and written by Margo XS, Zhone, Helena Gao and longtime collaborator MNEK, the album aligns closely with Larsson’s typical Euro-pop sound while incorporating deeper lyricism and aspects of electronic music. Larsson — best known for her 2015 single “Lush Life” and “Symphony,” her 2017 collaboration with Clean Bandit — [stated](https://www.clashmusic.com/news/zara-larsson-announces-new-album-midnight-sun/) that “Midnight Sun” “just feels like me — knowing myself, this album is just really, really me. And also, no one can do me the way I can.”
The album’s first and eponymous track, “Midnight Sun,” starts off the project with an upbeat, electro-pop energy that highlights Larsson’s strong vocals, a key feature of the album. “Blue Moon” keeps the same upbeat tone and production of the previous song, while “Saturn’s Return” — the penultimate track — continues the pattern of celestial-themed titles.

But “Saturn’s Return” is a much more serious and introspective track, both lyrically and production-wise. Larsson uses the track to reflect on her past mistakes and accept the uncertainty of the future. “I tried to control all that was unknown / ’Cause I was scared / Thought I could grow out of uncertainty / But instead I grew not to care,” she sings in the second verse.

 ADVERTISEMENT 

While not named after a celestial body, “The Ambition,” the album’s eighth track, takes a similar approach. While the track’s slow tempo is initially jarring in such an upbeat album, the lyrics fit in well with the theme of “Saturn’s Return.” Discussing how endlessly chasing success can be draining, especially in the music industry, Larsson sings, “I’m never satisfied ’cause I want number one / Doesn’t everyone?”

“Pretty Ugly” and “Hot & Sexy” take a different approach to production. Featuring a catchy, spoken chorus, “Pretty Ugly” feels more chaotic, looser and messier than the rest of the album. Larsson foreshadows this in the outro of the preceding track, “Blue Moon,” mentioning that she wants to “get messy … Like really messy” in a conversation with producer MNEK.

“Hot & Sexy” features a viral sound bite from TV personality Tiffany Pollard when she was on season 17 of Celebrity Big Brother UK. Pollard specially re-recorded a portion of her quote — “beautiful, fly, hot and sexy” — for Larsson’s song. Despite the fun, hedonistic energy of the track, Larsson sends an impactful message in the outro of “Hot & Sexy,” singing “Crime on womankind, scared to go outside / It still blows my mind how we just let it slide … There’s boys that need to be raised.”

On tracks like “Girl’s Girl” and “Crush,” the singer explores more vulnerable scenarios while keeping an upbeat electro-pop tone. In “Girl’s Girl,” Larsson plays the part of someone struggling to stay loyal to a close friend whose boyfriend she is in love with. On “Crush,” the singer explores the feelings of having a crush while already in a relationship. While both of the songs are a bit dated production-wise — more similar to Larsson’s hits from the late 2010s — they still have a clear, dynamic sound to them, making up for their antiquated feel.

“Puss Puss,” which translates to “Kiss Kiss” in Swedish, is the final track on the album. While the song is a symbolic way to close “Midnight Sun” — it’s about hanging up on a phone call — it leaves a bit more to be desired. Compared to other tracks on the album, “Puss Puss” is anticlimactic, although ethereal and sanguine. One would expect that on such a well-produced album, where each track seems to build upon the other, Larsson would either go fully introspective — like in “The Ambition” — or fully upbeat — like in “Midnight Sun” — but “Puss Puss” does neither.

Despite its minor flaws, “Midnight Sun” is undoubtedly a turning point in Larsson’s career. After almost two decades in the music industry, she has harnessed her strong vocals, Swedish cultural heritage and introspective songwriting to create her strongest project yet.

Zara Larsson, who won Sweden’s Got Talent at only 10-years-old, recently released her fifth studio album, “[Midnight Sun](https://open.spotify.com/album/0nte5x6fXd37Nt7jALSmx0).”

Larsson was the lead writer on this album but also got help from long-time collaborator and producer MNEK as well as fellow producers Margo XS, Zhone and Helena Gao.

“Midnight Sun” was released on Sept. 26, 2025, making it one of the best days of my year. With three head-banging singles and promotional videos that referenced 2000s nostalgia, it’s safe to say I was on the edge of my seat waiting for the album to drop.

The infectious album opens with its title track, “Midnight Sun,” which also served as the record's second single. This electropop anthem holds a lot of personal meaning to Larsson, drawing on her upbringing in Sweden, specifically how the sun never sets in summer months.

“Midnight Sun” is the perfect title track, with its summery beat and catchy chorus, this song represents what listeners can expect for the remainder of the album. This song also highlights the vocal growth that Larsson has done since her last album, “[VENUS](https://open.spotify.com/album/0qqZ6HD72So93exL9rH7zi).”

Following “Midnight Sun” is the track “Blue Moon,” an ethereal feeling song that maintains the captivating feeling of other tracks on this album. Although “Blue Moon” wasn’t originally one of my favorites, the song's siren-like qualities have since left me craving more. Specifically, the vocalizations towards the end of the song make it feel like I’m flying under the moon, which is probably the vibe Larsson and her producers were going for.

The lead single of the album “Pretty Ugly,” follows “Blue Moon.” This song takes a break from the ethereal sound of the previous song and leans into messy vocals and production, but in a fun and unique way. Besides “Pretty Ugly” being a very alternative sound for Larsson, the message of loving yourself even if society doesn’t, is one that Larsson has expressed in previous works.

“Pretty Ugly” is an earworm of a song, from shouting her lyrics to rapping them, Larsson has solidified her versatility when it comes to creating individualistic singles. I specifically love songs that are fun to shout, so it’s safe to say I’ve annoyed my roommates plenty of times by screaming the lyrics “Have you ever seen a pretty girl get ugly like this?”

“Girl’s Girl” is the fourth track in “Midnight Sun.” While this song is probably my least favorite on the album, that doesn’t make it a bad song. Larsson wrote “Girl’s Girl" in order to show her conflicting feelings toward her crush on her friend’s boyfriend and her identity as a girl’s girl, or someone who is praised for female solidarity and feminism.
The lyrics “I wanna be a girl’s girl, but what happens when a girl’s girl wants the boy,” sum up the general idea of this song. While I generally don’t enjoy either the lyrics or the message behind them, the beat is enough to keep me coming back for more.

Along the same lines of “Girl’s Girl” is the song “Crush,” the third and final single from the album. “Crush” is my favorite from the singles, it returns to the heavy electropop present in the song “Midnight Sun.”

“Crush” delves deeper into Larsson’s new infatuation with someone and how she's feeling crushed because of it. The lyrics, “Got me wonderin’ if it’s destiny or am I being messy,” make me question if this song is about the same man that’s dating her friend in the song “Girl’s Girl,” which would definitely be messy.

Up next is one of my favorites “Eurosummer.” This song switches up the vibe on the album by using traditionally European and Swedish sounds while still maintaining elements of dance-pop. The name of the song being “Eurosummer” fits perfectly considering that a European summer is exactly what it sounds like. The best movie to describe the sound of this song would be Pixar’s “[Luca](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-f28b825f-c207-406b-923a-67f85e6d90e0).”

Larsson talked about her inspirations for this album not only being Swedish summers, but also identity, self-reflection, ambition and of course, dancing, which leads me to the next song “Hot & Sexy.”

“Hot & Sexy” focuses on the dancing elements of this album; the lighthearted lyrics and electric production light a fire inside of me that can only be put out through dancing. My obsession with this album has led me to play it for anyone close to me, one thing I can confidently say is that people yearn for “Hot & Sexy.”

The theme of ambition makes its grand debut in the song entitled “The Ambition,” and how fitting. “The Ambition” was one of my personal favorites from my first listen.

This partially upbeat and catchy song will have you banging your head along, but don’t be fooled, “The Ambition” is a very personal song for Larsson. Lyrics such as “Yeah, it got me a lot, but that’s not good enough” and “I’ll keep breaking my heart if I can be your star” express how much Larsson is laying her heart on the table. She wants to be adored by fans and she won’t give up until she succeeds, after all, she was “raised on validation.”

The second to last song is titled “Saturn’s Return.” This song takes a break from the upbeat dance songs listeners have come to expect by returning to the ethereal, space-like production present in “Blue Moon.”

The beginning of “Saturn’s Return” feels very mysterious and builds up to the chorus which makes me feel like I might actually be able to fly. With its echoey quality and graceful vocals, the chorus in this song is hard to top. I find myself listening to “Saturn’s Return" when I get done with a long day of school and want to feel a little bit of peace when I return home.

The final song in Larsson's newest album is “Puss Puss,” which is Swedish for “Kiss Kiss.” This song closes off the album on a very good note by returning to Larsson’s signature dance-pop sound. This song talks about Larsson’s current partner and how she never wants to hang up the phone on them. The playful and confident sound of this song matches the raunchy lyrics and closes the album on a fun note that is very reminiscent of some of her previous hits.

Overall, this album feels like a warm day at the beach enhanced by a gentle breeze and your best friends. I can’t recommend any Zara Larsson album more than “Midnight Sun.” This album updates all of the catchy, upbeat bops from previous projects while infusing different aspects of personal moments from Larsson to create dance-pop perfection.

To keep up with Larsson and any future projects, be sure to follow her on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/zaralarsson/).

Zara Larsson Burns Through Sleepless Summer Nights on ‘Midnight Sun’
====================================================================

Swedish pop artist's high-energy fifth album mixes joy and confusion

By [Brittany Spanos](https://www.rollingstone.com/author/brittany-spanos/)

### [Brittany Spanos](https://www.rollingstone.com/author/brittany-spanos/)

[Contact Brittany Spanos on X](https://twitter.com/ohheybrittany "X Icon")

*   [What Are the Members of Måneskin Up To?](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/maneskin-members-thomas-raggi-album-1235475197/)
*   [Why Do Pop Stars Keep Threatening to Quit Pop Stardom?](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/pop-stars-done-with-stardom-charli-xcx-1235476218/)
*   [Amanda Seyfried, Daniel Blumberg Duet on ‘Clothed by the Sun’ From ‘The Testament of Ann Lee’ Film](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/amanda-seyfried-daniel-blumberg-clothed-by-the-sun-song-1235476177/)

[View all posts by Brittany Spanos](https://www.rollingstone.com/author/brittany-spanos/)

 September 26, 2025 

![Image 6: Zara Larsson](https://www.rollingstone.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/zara-larsson-midnight-sun-review.jpg?w=1581&h=1054&crop=1)

Zara Larsson Charlotte Rutherford*

Euro summer isn’t over if you don’t want it to be. Just ask [Zara Larsson](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/zara-larsson/), whose fifth album, _Midnight Sun,_ keeps the good vibes, long days, and late nights going. From start to finish, Larsson’s latest refuses to ever slow down, instead trafficking in high-energy dance-pop joy.

Hailing from pop mecca Sweden, Larsson wanted to celebrate the sun-drenched energy of a summer in her home country. Title track “Midnight Sun” is as deliriously hypnotic as the experience of partying through 24 hours of daylight. With notes of trance in its swirling chorus uplifted by Larsson’s extended run, the song is the perfect high-energy kickoff to the rest of the LP.

As the album progresses, Larsson jumps between the more sweet and sour emotions that percolate in the heat. Like “Midnight Sun,” songs like “Blue Moon,” “Euro Summer,” and “Puss Puss” (Swedish for “kiss kiss”) traffic in the sweetness: she waxes poetic through tender scenes of short sundresses, late-night phone calls and handprints left on her ass. But the more interesting moments are when she’s a little naughtier. On “Girl’s Girl,” she’s wracked with guilt for wanting a childhood-friend’s man. Meanwhile, over the stomp beat of “Pretty Ugly,” she threatens slashed tires and crashed cars. “Have you ever seen a pretty girl get ugly like this?” she threatens early on the track.

Trending Stories
----------------

[### 'SNL' Cold Open: Trump Reveals Why He's Putting His Name on Everything](https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/snl-cold-open-trump-reveals-jeffrey-epstein-name-buildings-1235488467/)[### Trump's DNA Dragnet: The Law That Turns Us All Into Suspects](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-features/trump-dna-dragnet-immigration-policy-biometric-surveillance-1235487564/)[### 'SNL' Weekend Update Roasts RFK Jr.'s Look, Trump's Epstein Files Redactions](https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-news/snl-weekend-update-roasts-rfk-jr-trump-jeffrey-epstein-1235488464/)[### AI Is Inventing Academic Papers That Don’t Exist — And They’re Being Cited in Real Journals](https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/ai-chatbot-journal-research-fake-citations-1235485484/)

The more complex, ugly feelings start to bleed into sleepless ruminations about her life. “The Ambition” pulls a few pages from the raw moments of Charli XCX’s _Brat_: Here Larsson yearns to be bigger, brighter. “But that’s the thing with the ambition/I want it so much/Everything’s a competition/So out of touch,” she declares on one of the biggest earworm moments of the project. “Saturn’s Return” is a standout in this vein, as the 27-year-old leans into life’s confusions, giving up control she sought when she was younger.

Those messier moments are where Larsson comes alive. You can hear her coming into her own across _Midnight Sun,_ where even her more formulaic moments still shine brighter than that Swedish summer sun. That ambition is paying off.

12.title: How Zara Larsson Made Summer Last Forever With ‘Midnight Sun’
12.description: Nearly a decade after her hit “Lush Life,” Larsson delivers her most radiant body of work and explains how it all came together.
12.content:
[Skip to main content](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/zara-larsson-breaks-down-midnight-sun-summer-forever-1235437954/#pagetop)[](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/zara-larsson-breaks-down-midnight-sun-summer-forever-1235437954/)

How Zara Larsson Made Summer Last Forever With ‘Midnight Sun’
-------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1: Zara Larsson](https://www.rollingstone.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/zara-larsson-interview.jpg?w=1581&h=1054&crop=1)

Zara Larsson Charlotte Rutherford*

The night [Zara Larsson](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/zara-larsson/)’s _[Midnight Sun](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/zara-larsson-midnight-sun-review-1235435727/)_ dropped, the singer’s closest friends, collaborators (and even a few Katseye members) packed into a Los Angeles bar to watch her blow out candles as the album officially arrived. The Swedish midnight sun she sings about wasn’t shining, but Larsson was.

“I feel like I rarely do that,” she tells _Rolling Stone_ the following morning. “I am so bad at celebrating milestones and accomplishments. I don’t even like celebrating my birthday. It was nice to come together in a room and remind ourselves that we made it.”

_Midnight Sun_ has reignited Larsson’s pop stardom in ways beyond even her own imagination. Nearly a decade after “Lush Life” and “Never Forget You” first launched her onto the global stage, the Swedish star is stepping into a new era. At 27, Larsson is reveling in long-overdue recognition — and finally basking in the spotlight her fans always knew she deserved.

A [_Rolling Stone_ review](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/zara-larsson-midnight-sun-review-1235435727/)of the album gave it four stars, lauding it for “refusing to ever slow down, instead trafficking in high-energy dance-pop joy.” Larsson admits to me that she read the review, and seeing the positive reception for the record has put a smile on her face — even if she isn’t allowing critical acclaim to dictate her happiness.

“I used to search my name on Twitter, and Google my name… This time, I, of course, want people to love it just as much as I do, but I am so proud of it. I’m really happy about this body of work,” she says. “I just have confidence in what we’ve created and how it feels for me, but it does feel great to have that sense of accomplishment validated.”

It’s been a long time coming. Pop stans will argue the rollout for _Midnight Sun_ — inspired by the endless summer evenings in her native Sweden — began more than a year ago, even if it wasn’t Larsson’s doing. Last summer, TikTok users revived her Clean Bandit collab “[Symphony](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/zara-larsson-dolphin-symphony-meme-clean-bandit-explained-1235098869/),” pairing it with surreal clips of dolphins flying through a Lisa Frank–like world. The posts were bizarre, but they put Larsson back in the pop conversation. And as she rolled out the new album, she leaned into that momentum, weaving it into a vibrant aesthetic defined by ultra-bright palettes and a Y2K-inspired, optimism-soaked style that matched the summery spirit of the project she’s made.

Editor’s picks
--------------

It’s been an impressive last year for Larsson, who spent the summer going viral for her performances and bubbly personality, reintroducing fans to a pop star fully in her element — giddy to deliver the full pop persona, no holds barred. She just wrapped an opening slot for [Tate McRae](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/tate-mcrae-so-close-to-what-review-1235275458/), where her choreography-packed performances shot through TikTok every night, and she’s gearing up for her own tour. First, she’ll fill arenas across Europe and then hit Jingle Ball in the U.S. before a massive 2026 run that promises to make the _Midnight Sun_ era burn longer and brighter.

Some of the songs on _Midnight Sun_ reflect an introspective side of Larsson, who goes from partying on “Pretty Ugly” and Crush” to speaking her truth about grappling with the ideas of success on “Saturn’s Return” and “The Ambition.” She says with a giggle: “It’s playful and fun, and also it has layers to it.”

From the back of an SUV in Los Angeles, Larsson breaks down five of her favorite tracks from the new album, describes how she got Tiffany Pollard to re-record one of her most viral memes, and explains why turning 27 might have changed her brain chemistry.

**Midnight Sun**
----------------

The title track sets the tone of the album. It’s melodic. It’s dance-y. It has this Jersey Club beat. I always wanted to write a song called “Midnight Sun.” I just loved the symbolism of it. I’ve tried it for five times and nothing really stuck. But, this time around, we fucking made it work. That was one of the first songs that we did for the project where it felt, “Oh, okay, this is definitely something.” And, on the same day, we did “Pretty Ugly,” so we were, like, “Huh, this is a fucking success. This is the energy right now. This is my album. This is what it’s going to be.” I’m just so happy about it and how it turned out. I finally have my perfect midnight sun song.

Related Content
---------------

**Eurosummer**
--------------

I like this being like a Eurovision song, like 2012 Romania or something. Do you remember “Mr. Saxobeat” by Alexandra Stan? Or “Hot” by INNA? It’s that Eastern European, almost Mediterranean vibe of just summer to me. The accordion, I just wanted to play with that because that to me is summer, and it’s nostalgic and it’s fun. I think that’s something that is just a part of who I am as a person and why I thought it was important to like, “How can I put my identity more into this album?” It’s camp. It’s fun. It’s silly, but so entertaining.I’m not going to be a part of Eurovision, but I can flirt with it. We take Eurovision so, so, so seriously. When people come over to Europe and have like a Eurosummer, it’s usually in the southern part of Europe, but it could also be in a tourist town in Croatia. It feels like me 10 shots in, me going to Turkey being 16. That’s also Eurosummer for me.

**Hot & Sexy**
--------------

“Hot & Sexy” is the bridge between “euphoric and fun” and “introspective” on the album because it’s about going out with your girlfriends, having a good time, being a bad bitch, looking good, and just being hot and sexy, feeling yourself, feeling, like, “Oh, yes.” And then we mashed that song with another song that we wrote earlier called “Let The Girl Live,” which is just about like, “Can a woman just live? Like, oh, my gosh, why do people have so many opinions? We want to be hot and sexy.”

The fact that Tiffany Pollard is on it is so iconic to me because she’s literally the internet. To me, she’s the ultimate queen of reality TV and giving you a read just effortlessly. I remember MNEK played me this track, and I was, like, “Oh, no, this is too good.” We just like hit her up and asked her if she wanted to come to the studio and just re-record it, And she was, like, “Yeah, I’ll come.” She was so cute and lovely. It’s not even a sample from Big Brother UK. It’s a re-recording of that iconic segment. She’s in the studio with her headphones and just, like, “Beautiful, fly, hot, sexy, thank you.” Ten minutes, in and out, we were, like, “Amazing.”

Trending Stories
----------------

**The Ambition**
----------------

I feel like I’ve always been super open and honest about, like, “I want to be a superstar. I want to have a big stage, and I want to have a big production.” And if it’s not happening now, then it will just happen later because I will keep releasing albums and songs and do what I love. In “The Ambition,” I’m like, “Will it ever really, truly be enough, or will my goalpost just keep changing?” I’m at a point where maybe the most important thing in my life isn’t to travel around and around and around and around. Maybe it’s about settling down, which is something I never thought of being a teenager. Like, “Wait. Maybe I want a family, and maybe I don’t want to just be on the road all the time. Maybe I want to have stability and settle down,” which is like kind of a scary thought because, if I’m not a pop star, then what is my purpose? I don’t know. And that’s Ok. Life changes. And, in a way, that’s the beautiful thing about it. It’s not supposed to be static. Sometimes you ask: “Life is so long. Am I a failure if I abandon my dream or if it becomes something else?” I feel like I know myself as a person a lot more now than when I was 20 or 17. I know more who I am. My roots are deeper, but then also that can maybe allow my leaves to change. To be clear: I think I’m going to be singing forever just because I just love to sing. That’s my passion, but there’s also so much more to life.

**Saturn’s Return**
-------------------

That one was the last song we made for the album. We were really supposed to finish. Margo, Helena, MNEK, and Zhone, we were just like, “Look, guys, we’re all here. Shouldn’t we just like make a song? Come on.” At that point, I was obsessed with the moon. I was reading about star signs and stuff, which I’m not really involved in, but, at that point, I was, like, “No. I feel something is shifting. I feel something is changing.” Saturn’s Return is when the planet goes back to where it was by the time you were born, which takes 27 years, and just how that’s a way of really coming into adulthood. I truly feel like I have changed a lot. Something in me has shifted just over the past year in how I move with everything in my life. It has made me very just humble towards life and how I’m just open to a lot of things, new perspectives, and see things from different sides. I think a part of it is like surrendering to life while also trying to do the best you can and be the best version of yourself. Life takes you on a journey and you can never really predict what it’s going to be. And I don’t know what it’s going to be, and that’s kind of nice.

Zara Larsson earns career high with ‘Midnight Sun’
==================================================

*   [![Image 3: Buddy Iahn](https://themusicuniverse.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/buddynew-96x96.png)](https://themusicuniverse.com/author/buddyiahn/)[Buddy Iahn](https://themusicuniverse.com/author/buddyiahn/ "Posts by Buddy Iahn")

*   [Pop](https://themusicuniverse.com/category/news/pop/)

![Image 4: Zara Larsson earns career high with ‘Midnight Sun’](https://themusicuniverse.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/zaralarssonmidnight.jpg)

Epic Records

#### The album storms the charts as she earns new RIAA certifications

Zara Larsson’s never-ending [_Midnight Sun_](https://themusicuniverse.com/zara-larsson-announces-midnight-sun-album-tour/) is just getting started. With career-bests across the board, the multi-platinum global pop powerhouse celebrates several career highs.

_Midnight Sun,_ released via Sommer House/Epic Records,achieves a career-best debut at No. 3 on the Billboard Top Dance Albums chart, as well as in the top 25 of the Billboard Top Album Sales chart, landing at No. 22. She also lands No. 7 on Luminate’s Current Pop Albums chart, No. 10 on Internet Albums, and is Top 20 on the Digital Albums chart. “Crush,” in addition, is currently Top 20 at radio on the Pop Published chart. Alongside _Midnight Sun_’s momentum, Larsson has reached several new milestones as she surpasses 10.5 billion streams. New certification from the RIAA across Zara’s catalogue includes quadruple platinum for “Never Forget You,” triple platinum for “Lush Life,” and Gold for “Wow,” “I Would Like,” “All The Time,” and “I Can’t Fall In Love Without You.”

After wrapping up a stage and internet-conquering run on Tate McRae’s Miss Possessive Tour, the star will headline her multi-continent tour. Early demand has prompted venue upgrades in several markets, as well as second nights added in Los Angeles at The Wiltern on March 5, 2026, and in New York at the Brooklyn Paramount Theatre on March 27, 2026. The tour is set to kick off on October 28, 2025, in Munich, Germany, with stops along the way at London’s Wembley Arena and a hometown show at Stockholm’s Avicii Arena before arriving stateside in February 2026. Additionally, Larsson is set to perform across this year’s iHeartRadio Jingle Ball Tour.

Unapologetically unfiltered and openly vulnerable, _Midnight Sun_’s ten songs pulse with confidence, blending kaleidoscopic pop and euphoric dance to match every shade of Zara’s mood. Written with Helena Gao and producers MNEK, Margo XS, and Zhone, it draws from nearly 20 years in the spotlight. The album reveals all sides of the 27-year-old artist — lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain — often within the same breath. Standout tracks like the heartfelt anthem “Blue Moon,” the bold, genre-bending “Hot & Sexy,” the euphoric “Eurosummer,” and the introspective duo of “The Ambition” and “Saturn’s Return,” showcase Zara’s raw honesty as she explores love, autonomy, ambition, identity, and self-discovery. The new tracks join already-viral singles “Crush” and “Pretty Ugly,” as well as the world-conquering title track “Midnight Sun.”

Zara Larsson’s ‘Midnight Sun’ is her best body of work yet — Album Review
=========================================================================

 

[Album Reviews](https://www.melodicmag.com/category/album-reviews/)

 

By: [Germano Blanco](https://www.melodicmag.com/author/germanoblanco/)

 Date:

 

September 29, 2025

 

![Image 4: Midnight Sun Album Cover Art](https://www.melodicmag.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/midnightsun_albumcoverart-500x500.jpg)

Midnight Sun Album Cover Art

**Recommended tracks:** “Midnight Sun,” “Crush,” “Saturn’s Return”**Artists you may like:** [Tate McRae](https://www.melodicmag.com/?s=tate+mcrae), Jess Glynne, [KATSEYE](https://www.melodicmag.com/?s=katseye)

**[Zara Larsson](https://www.melodicmag.com/?s=zara+larsson)** told _[Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/zara-larsson-midnight-sun-interview-podcast-2025-album-1235364489/)_ back in June that she wanted to be the biggest pop star on the planet — even if just for a moment. While the Swedish singer-songwriter has been in the spotlight for over a decade with global hits such as 2017’s “Symphony” with Clean Bandit and 2015’s “Never Forget You” with MNEK (also a producer on this record), her most recent efforts failed to match her early success. With the release of her fifth studio album, [_Midnight Sun_](https://www.melodicmag.com/news/zara-larsson-announces-fifth-album-midnight-sun-and-fall-tour-dates/), it feels as though she is about to change that narrative.

The LP opens full of energy with the title track, setting the tone for the rest of the album. “Midnight Sun” transports you into a sunny dream you don’t want to wake up from, with trance-inspired production and Larsson’s hypnotizing voice; more specifically, _that_ vocal run on the chorus. On the second track, “Blue Moon,” she keeps the party going with another club-ready song in which she sings about blissful moments with a romantic partner.

“Pretty Ugly,” the lead single, arrives like a kick in the door as Larsson chants the chorus: “Have you ever seen a pretty girl get ugly like this? / Messy like this? / Losin’ her shit?” It sounds like a rebellious cheerleader anthem for women who are tired of gender expectations. In the verses, she sings, “Everybody’s tellin’ me to sit there really pretty / But I’m feelin’ like I wanna cause some trouble in the city tonight / Fuck the ladylike, more like crazy-like.”

While “Pretty Ugly” could be considered a feminist statement, the follow-up, “Girl’s Girl” flips the script on what that term normally means. Larsson playfully questions her own loyalty as she fantasizes about a girlfriend’s partner, singing, “I wanna be a girl’s girl / But what happens when a girl’s girl wants the boy? / I know that she’s my friend, but I just can’t avoid / The way I feel about you.”

“Crush” is by far the highlight of the project, an irresistible percussive pop jam that peaks with a showstopping bridge and an unexpected change in chord progression. Here, Larsson gives us the catchiest chorus of the album as she laments about not being able to be with her crush for fear of ruining her current relationship.

Reminiscent of [Don Omar](https://www.melodicmag.com/?s=don+omar)’s “Danza Kuduro” and Edward Maya & Vika Jigulina’s “Stereo Love,” the next track, “Eurosummer,” brings in new sonic textures with its accordion instrumentation. Likewise, in the confidence booster “Hot & Sexy,” which samples an audio clip of reality TV star Tiffany Pollard from _Celebrity Big Brother_, the production takes a turn in the second half of the song with a Brazilian funk break.

Before becoming too repetitive with the lyrical themes, Larsson switches things up with “The Ambition,” showing vulnerability perhaps for the first time in the record. Although it’s far from being a ballad, the singer opens up about how success has dictated her happiness and how comparison to other artists in the music industry feels inevitable. In the verses, she sings, “Raised on validation / Consumed by aspiration / Numbers meaning more than words / But what’s it worth?”

In “Saturn’s Return,” she pulls us in even closer by reflecting on how her life and aspirations have changed as she approaches her Saturn return, a term used in astrology to refer to the turbulent times of a person’s late twenties. Larsson shows emotional maturity by recognizing the uncertainty that comes with becoming an adult, singing, “And it feels so good to know I don’t know what I’m doing / And I love that I’m free in my naivety, I won’t lose it / Could be wrong, could be right / But this song is mine.”

“Saturn’s Return” would have been the perfect closing to the album, as Larsson’s heavenly falsetto in the end, followed by a cosmic-like synth pad, mirrors the dreamy feeling throughout the record. Instead, “Puss Puss,” the final track, while a fun and flirty encore, feels deeply misplaced and somewhat unmemorable.

Nonetheless, _Midnight Sun_ is a beautifully executed electro-pop LP with a distinctive yet familiar sound, which makes it feel both fresh and classic at the same time. The project proves that Zara Larsson might be well over a decade into her career, but she is still pushing herself to sonically evolve as an artist by exploring different genres within the dance-pop sphere. As a result, she delivers her strongest and most cohesive body of work yet while simultaneously finding a sound that feels true and unique to her, a hard feat to achieve in this new age of pop stars.

Midnight Sun *** **<br>Blue Moon *** **<br>Pretty Ugly *** **<br>Girl's Girl *** **<br>Crush *** **<br>Eurosummer *** ***<br>Hot & Sexy *** **<br>The Ambition *** *<br>Saturns Return *** **<br>Puss Puss *** **<br><br>5.0 - 5*<br><br>Seit ihrem grossen Durchbruch vor fast zehn Jahren ist Zara Larsson einfach ein Garant für starke Pop-Musik, ihr neuestes Album Midnight Sun ist dabei keine Ausnahme. Zara Larsson Earns Career Highs With 'Midnight Sun'
===================================================

* * *

 10-08-2025

* * *

![Image 9: Zara Larsson Earns Career Highs With 'Midnight Sun'](https://www.antimusic.com/news/photos/25/10/08/zara-larsson.jpg)

Play Zara Larsson 

 on Amazon Music Unlimited (ad)

(Epic) Zara Larsson's never-ending Midnight Sun is just getting started. With career-bests across the board, the multi-platinum global pop powerhouse celebrates several career highs.

Midnight Sun achieves a career-best debut at #3 on the Billboard Top Dance Albums chart, as well as in the top 25 of the Billboard Top Album Sales chart, landing at #22. She also lands #7 on Luminate's Current Pop Albums chart, #10 on Internet Albums, and is Top 20 on the Digital Albums chart.

"Crush," in addition, is currently Top 20 at radio on the Pop Published chart. Alongside Midnight Sun's momentum, Zara Larsson has reached several new milestones as she surpasses 10.5 billion streams. New certification from the RIAA across Zara's catalogue include 4x Platinum for "Never Forget You," 3x Platinum for "Lush Life" and Gold for "Wow," "I Would Like," "All The Time," and "I Can't Fall In Love Without You."
